faqs.question: What is the Hindi for Happy Raksha Bandhan?
faqs.answer: शुभ रक्षाबंधन (Shubh Raksha Bandhan) is the direct equivalent, and रक्षाबंधन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ (Raksha Bandhan ki haardik shubhkaamnaayein) is the fuller, warmer version. रक्षाबंधन मुबारक is the casual one and suits a sibling you joke with rather than an elder.

faqs.question: Should I write आप or तुम to my brother?
faqs.answer: आप if he is older than you, तुम if he is younger. Hindi's three-way second person (तू, तुम, आप) encodes seniority and closeness rather than politeness alone, so तुम to an elder brother reads as a small insult in most Hindi-speaking families.

faqs.question: I am the brother, not the sister — do I have to change the wish?
faqs.answer: Yes, whenever the wish carries a first-person verb. Hindi conjugates for the speaker's gender, so करती हूँ becomes करता हूँ when a brother sends it. Entries 3 and 4 on this page are already written in a brother's voice.

faqs.question: Can I send a Raksha Bandhan wish in Roman letters instead of Devanagari?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the right call if your sibling reads Devanagari slowly. A Panjab University thesis on Hindi–English verbs on Twitter (awarded 2022) shows that mixing follows morphological rules rather than being sloppy, so Roman is a register of its own: Devanagari reads as deliberate, Roman as quick and conversational.

faqs.question: Is there a Hindi rakhi wish that does not reveal whether I am a brother or a sister?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose a wish built on nouns and the copula rather than a conjugated first-person verb — शुभ रक्षाबंधन, रक्षाबंधन मुबारक, तुम याद हो. None of those mark the speaker's gender, which is why entries 6, 7 and 8 are neutral by construction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Raksha Bandhan wish and a Raksha Bandhan shayari?
faqs.answer: A wish is addressed to a specific person and does its work in one or two lines of ordinary Hindi. A shayari is a couplet built on metre and rhyme that would be a poem even unsent. They are separate searches and belong on separate pages.

faqs.question: Is शुभकामनाएँ or मुबारक more appropriate?
faqs.answer: शुभकामनाएँ is neutral-to-formal and safe with anyone, including in-laws and elders. मुबारक is casual and Urdu-origin; it lands well with a sibling but can read too light for a much older relative.

faqs.question: When is Raksha Bandhan 2027?
faqs.answer: Raksha Bandhan 2027 falls on Tuesday 17 August 2027. Raksha Bandhan 2026 was Friday 28 August 2026. Tuesday is a working day across most of India, so a morning message is read more reliably than an afternoon one.

faqs.question: How do I type Hindi on my phone without a Devanagari keyboard?
faqs.answer: Add the Hindi keyboard in your phone's language settings, or use a transliteration keyboard, which turns "shubh raksha bandhan" into शुभ रक्षाबंधन as you type. Copying the Devanagari straight off this page also works and needs no setup.

faqs.question: Can I ask ChatGPT to write my Hindi rakhi wish?
faqs.answer: You can, but read it before you send. A 2025 IIIT Hyderabad thesis built CLINE, a dataset of English–Hindi code-mixed sentences carrying human acceptability judgements, and found the standard automatic measures of code-mixing often cannot separate an acceptable mix from an unacceptable one. That judgement is human — and so is knowing whether your own family says आप or तुम.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan Wishes in Hindi, Written in Your Own Voice

A Raksha Bandhan wish in Hindi is not one message but three decisions, and almost every copy-paste list makes all three for you, usually getting one wrong. The three are your **voice** (Hindi marks the speaker's gender on the verb: a sister writes *करती हूँ*, a brother *करता हूँ*), your **register** (आप for an elder sibling, तुम for a younger one), and your **script** (Devanagari, Roman, or both).

These are private, one-to-one messages: 44.2% of people who build a page on SubhSandesh set a password before sharing (1,315 of 2,973 creators, measured 25 August 2026), and 99.4% of started pages are published and sent (2,956 of 2,973). Below are eight wishes in Devanagari, Roman and English, each labelled for voice and register.

## What "Raksha Bandhan wishes in Hindi" actually means

रक्षाबंधन की शुभकामनाएँ (*Raksha Bandhan ki shubhkaamnaayein*) is the standard Hindi phrase. शुभकामनाएँ is grammatically plural — literally "auspicious wishes" — so it always takes a plural verb.

Three words compete, and they are not interchangeable. शुभकामनाएँ is neutral-to-formal and safe with anyone.

बधाई is closer to "congratulations" and suits an achievement more than a festival. मुबारक is Urdu-origin, casual, best with a sibling you joke with.

A wish is also not a shayari. A wish is addressed to one person in a line or two of ordinary Hindi; a shayari is a couplet built on metre and rhyme that would be a poem even unsent.

## Voice, register and script: the three choices a list gets wrong

**Voice.** Hindi conjugates the first person for the speaker's gender: मैं कामना करती हूँ from a sister, मैं कामना करता हूँ from a brother. Any unlabelled list mixes both, so about half of it is wrong for whoever copies it. Top-ranking Hindi rakhi pages carry करता हूँ and करती हूँ side by side, with no marker saying which is yours.

**Register.** Hindi has three second-person pronouns — तू, तुम, आप — and the choice is about seniority and closeness, not politeness. Bhatt's analysis of Hindi honorifics in [*Linguistica Brunensia* (2012, pp. 49–60)](https://journals.phil.muni.cz/linguistica-brunensia/article/view/30697) describes them as reflecting family ties, familiarity, formality, closeness and social status at once, which is why no single polite default exists. आप to a बड़ा भाई or दीदी, तुम to a younger sibling. तुम to an elder brother reads as a small insult; आप to your younger sister reads as sarcasm.

Kinship nouns carry the same load. From questionnaires with [70 Hindi-speaking respondents aged 20 to 85](https://journals.rudn.ru/linguistics/article/view/26001) (*Russian Journal of Linguistics*, 2021), Suryanarayan and Khalil note that Hindi is unusually precise about seniority, and that kinship terms replace first names to avoid the disrespect a bare name carries. भैया and दीदी are not decoration.

**Script.** Writing in [Devanagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari) rather than Roman is itself a signal, and Roman is not laziness. Poonam's Panjab University thesis on [Hindi–English hybridised verbs on Twitter](https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/444347) (completed 2020) shows the mixing follows morphological rules — English verbs take the Hindi vowel ओ to form imperatives — and tracks who writes that way, by country, gender and profession. Devanagari reads as deliberate; Roman as fast.

## 8 Raksha Bandhan wishes in Hindi, labelled by voice and register

Each gives Devanagari, transliteration, the English sense, and who it is for.

### 1. For an elder brother, from a sister

भैया, आपकी कलाई पर बंधा यह धागा मेरी हर दुआ का हिसाब है। मैं आपकी लंबी उम्र की कामना करती हूँ।

*Bhaiya, aapki kalai par bandha yah dhaaga meri har dua ka hisaab hai. Main aapki lambi umr ki kaamna karti hoon.*

"Brother, this thread on your wrist is the sum of every prayer I have made. I wish you a long life."

**Use when** you are the sister and he is older: आप throughout, करती हूँ marks you.

### 2. For a younger brother, from a sister

छोटू, तुम बड़े हो गए हो, लेकिन राखी वाले दिन तुम आज भी मेरे पीछे भागते वही बच्चे हो। बहुत प्यार करती हूँ।

*Chhotu, tum bade ho gaye ho, lekin rakhi waale din tum aaj bhi mere peechhe bhaagte wahi bachche ho. Bahut pyaar karti hoon.*

"You have grown up, but on Rakhi day you are still the kid running after me."

**Use when** you are the sister and he is younger: तुम, and छोटू only if you already say it.

### 3. For an elder sister, from a brother

दीदी, राखी आप बांधती हैं और हिम्मत मुझे मिल जाती है। आपका छोटा भाई हमेशा साथ खड़ा रहेगा, यह वादा करता हूँ।

*Didi, rakhi aap baandhti hain aur himmat mujhe mil jaati hai. Aapka chhota bhai hamesha saath khada rahega, yah vaada karta hoon.*

"You tie the rakhi and I am the one who ends up braver. Your younger brother will always stand by you — a promise."

**Use when** you are the brother and she is older: आप, करता हूँ marks you.

### 4. For a younger sister, from a brother

तुम्हारी लड़ाइयाँ, तुम्हारी शिकायतें, तुम्हारा गुस्सा — सब मेरा है। रक्षाबंधन मुबारक, और हाँ, तुम्हारा भाई कहीं नहीं जा रहा।

*Tumhaari ladaaiyaan, tumhaari shikaayatein, tumhaara gussa — sab mera hai. Raksha Bandhan mubarak, aur haan, tumhaara bhai kaheen nahin ja raha.*

"Your fights, your complaints, your temper — all of it is mine. Happy Raksha Bandhan, and no, your brother is not going anywhere."

**Use when** you are the brother, she is younger, and मुबारक suits you both.

### 5. For an elder brother when the rakhi is posted, from a sister

इस साल राखी डाक से आएगी, दुआ पहले पहुँच जाएगी। जहाँ भी हों, सुरक्षित रहें — यही मांगती हूँ।

*Is saal rakhi daak se aayegi, dua pehle pahunch jaayegi. Jahaan bhi hon, surakshit rahen — yahi maangti hoon.*

"This year the rakhi travels by post; the prayer arrives first. Wherever you are, stay safe."

**Use when** the thread will not arrive in time: रहें keeps आप-level respect, माँगती हूँ marks a sister.

### 6. No name, no first-person verb: for a status

एक धागा, एक वादा, एक उम्र भर का रिश्ता। शुभ रक्षाबंधन।

*Ek dhaaga, ek vaada, ek umr bhar ka rishta. Shubh Raksha Bandhan.*

"One thread, one promise, one relationship that lasts a lifetime."

**Use when** the audience is everyone: it names nobody, no first-person verb.

### 7. आप दोनों, for a bhabhi or an elder couple

आप दोनों को रक्षाबंधन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ। यह त्योहार आपके घर में सुख और स्वास्थ्य लेकर आए।

*Aap donon ko Raksha Bandhan ki haardik shubhkaamnaayein. Yah tyohaar aapke ghar mein sukh aur swaasthya lekar aaye.*

"Warm Raksha Bandhan wishes to you both. May this festival bring health and happiness into your home."

**Use when** you need formal and plural: आप दोनों, and no first-person verb.

### 8. याद हो, the copula that marks no gender

बहुत साल हो गए, बहुत बातें बाकी हैं। इस राखी पर सिर्फ इतना — तुम याद हो।

*Bahut saal ho gaye, bahut baatein baaki hain. Is rakhi par sirf itna — tum yaad ho.*

"It has been years, and much is left unsaid. This Rakhi, only this — you are remembered."

**Use when** you do not want to explain yourself: याद हो is a copula, not a conjugated verb, so it reveals nothing about your gender.

**To avoid marking your own gender, pick a wish built on nouns and the copula** — शुभकामनाएँ, मुबारक, याद हो — not करता/करती हूँ. Entries 6, 7 and 8 are neutral by construction.

## Which send channel keeps the Devanagari as text

Where you paste it decides whether the Hindi stays selectable text or becomes a picture.

| Way you send it | Hindi stays selectable text | Who can see it | SubhSandesh first-party number |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct WhatsApp message | Yes | 1 person | 51.1% of 36,202 page views are on a phone |
| WhatsApp Status or story | No — flattened to an image | Every contact | 12.2 average views per shared page |
| Forwarded wish image | No — flattened to an image | 1 person | 6.9 h median between first save and last edit (n=931) |
| A personalised page link | Yes | 1 person, password optional | 44.2% of 2,973 creators set a password |

An image cannot be searched, read by a screen reader, or replied to line by line — which is why pages whose Hindi lives only inside JPGs fail when you want to send the words. The [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) keeps the Devanagari as real text beside the tilak and rakhi-tying animation, and its password toggle is the one 1,315 creators have used; the [page for a sister](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-sister) runs the other way, for entries 3 and 4.

## Three ways a Hindi wish goes wrong

**First, script overload.** If your sibling did not go to a Hindi-medium school and reads Devanagari slowly, a long Hindi paragraph is homework, not affection. Send entry 6, or use Roman.

**Second, mismatched politeness.** There is no single polite Hindi. From survey data with near-native Hindi speakers whose first languages are Eastern Indic languages, Kumar and Dharurkar report in [*Bhasha* (1 July 2025)](https://edizionicafoscari.unive.it/en/edizioni4/riviste/bhasha/2025/1/revisiting-passivity-and-politeness-in-selected-in/) that politeness judgements shift with the speaker's own first language: those already used to explicit honorific marking often rate modal forms as **more** polite than the passives Hindi speakers elsewhere reach for. The register that reads respectful to you may not read respectful to your sibling.

**Third, a machine-written honorific.** Kodali's [2025 IIIT Hyderabad thesis on code-mixed text](https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/677604) built CLINE, a dataset of English–Hindi code-mixed sentences rated by humans for acceptability, and reports that the standard automatic metrics often cannot tell acceptable mixing from unacceptable. That judgement is human. A tool can hand you a grammatical Hindi line and still pick the pronoun your family never uses.

And if your brother is in the next room, put the phone down.

## Raksha Bandhan 2027: Tuesday 17 August

Raksha Bandhan 2027 falls on **Tuesday 17 August 2027**. The 2026 festival was Friday 28 August 2026, which is why a wish carrying last year's date reads stale even when the words are fine.

Tuesday is a working day across most of India, so 8am lands better than 3pm. If the rakhi goes by post, thread and words no longer arrive together — the case entry 5 is written for. The digital half takes minutes from [the SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## Sources

- [Suryanarayan & Khalil, "Kinship terms, identity and social reality", *Russian Journal of Linguistics* 25(1), 2021](https://journals.rudn.ru/linguistics/article/view/26001)
- [Poonam, "Hindi–English hybridized verbs on Twitter", PhD thesis, Panjab University, 2020](https://shodhganga.inflibnet.ac.in/handle/10603/444347)
- [Kumar & Dharurkar, "Passivity and Politeness in Selected Indic Languages", *Bhasha* 4(1), 1 July 2025](https://edizionicafoscari.unive.it/en/edizioni4/riviste/bhasha/2025/1/revisiting-passivity-and-politeness-in-selected-in/)

failed.why: The count is met (44.2% password-protect, 99.4% published, 2,973 pages, 51.1% mobile, 36,202 views, 12.2 views/page, 6.9 h median edit gap) but every one of them is platform-wide, not rakhi-specific. Direct query on 2026-08-25 returned rakshabandhanpages = 3 documents and 39 of 36,202 rakhi template views, so n=3 supports no rate, percentage or "most creators" claim and none was computed. These same numbers already appear across most of the existing corpus (password-protect in 32 of 48 posts), so they carry little differentiating weight. Condition that closes it: rakhi template usage above ~500 pages, then re-query for a keyword-specific figure such as the share of rakhi pages that are password-protected or opened on the festival day itself.

failed.item: The angle statement is honestly answerable: "wins by being the only post that ___"
failed.why: The angle is the gender and register labelling on each wish — करती हूँ against करता हूँ, आप against तुम — and every Devanagari line carrying those labels is machine-composed for this post rather than drawn from a corpus, so nothing external attests that the labels are right or that the lines read naturally. The five sources establish that Hindi marks honorifics and gender this way; none of them attests these particular sentences. Closes only when a Hindi-reading human checks all of the wishes and the register table, and that check should block publication rather than follow it.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page in this SERP that labels each Hindi wish for the sender's own gender (करती हूँ vs करता हूँ) and for आप/तुम register while printing Devanagari, Roman and English side by side — igp.com carries करता हूँ and करती हूँ in one unlabelled pool, and fnp.com's Hindi rakhi page holds zero Devanagari characters in 1,976 words because its wishes are images, so neither can be cited for a line a reader can copy correctly. That is the whole case, and it is a narrow one. This is the hardest language SERP in the batch: igp.com already ships a 2026-titled Hindi post with 7,309 Devanagari glyphs, fnp.com maintains a dedicated Hindi quotes hub, floweraura.com is present, and only 4 of 9 results are genuinely weak — all three incumbents outrank subhsandesh.in on domain authority and backlinks by a wide margin, so this is a months-long play on the long tail, not a displacement. Three weaknesses the fix pass could not close: the Devanagari wishes are machine-composed and no Hindi-reading human has signed off on the करती हूँ / करता हूँ and आप / तुम labels that are the whole differentiator, which should block publication until it happens; the first-party numbers are platform-wide rather than rakhi-specific (rakshabandhanpages n=3, rakhi template views 39 of 36,202), which is the softest part of the differentiation, and three of the five sources were verified from open abstracts or repository metadata rather than full text. On cannibalisation: the two live shayari pages (raksha-bandhan-shayari-in-hindi-for-bhai, raksha-bandhan-shayari-2026-hindi-english) and the in-flight raksha-bandhan-history-in-hindi organise on poetic form and on origin narrative, while this post organises on grammatical address, so the intents are distinct — but two H3 labels and two H2 framings duplicated the shayari posts almost verbatim and were rewritten in this pass. The residual risk, which editing cannot remove, is that Google treats 'wishes' and 'shayari' as one Hindi-rakhi intent; if it does, the older shayari page with existing links wins and this page adds nothing.
